title: Custom business apps
seoTitle: Custom Business Apps, Websites & Automation | EfiOps
metaDescription: Outgrown spreadsheets and disconnected tools? EfiOps reviews how your business works, then builds connected websites, admin dashboards, automations and useful AI.
h1: Your business has grown. Your systems should catch up.
eyebrow: Business review → A focused plan → A connected system
lead: The same details entered twice. Quotes chased from memory. A website that stops at the contact form. Let’s find what is slowing your business down, then build the tools that move it forward.

sections.heading: Your team shouldn’t be the connection between every system.
paragraphs: A customer sends a request. Someone copies it into a spreadsheet. Someone else creates a quote. The job details move into another tool. When the customer asks for an update, you search the inbox to piece it together.

Each workaround seems small. Together, they take attention away from customers, make ownership unclear and leave important work dependent on memory. We start by finding those gaps in your actual process.

sections.heading: Build the missing connections. Keep what already works.
paragraphs: The right answer might be a better website, a shared dashboard, an integration or a custom application. You don’t have to choose the technology before we understand the work.
items: A website that starts the right conversation. Clear services, useful forms and a route into your internal workflow.
An admin dashboard that shows what needs attention. Customer records, job stages, owners, next actions and relevant reporting in one working view.
Automations that move routine work forward. Capture a request, create a task, ask for approval or flag a delay, with visible failures and a manual fallback.
Customer portals where they earn their place. Give customers controlled access to agreed progress, documents or actions without exposing internal records.
AI with a defined job. Help search approved knowledge, summarise a request or prepare a draft, with permissions and human review where needed.
sections.caption: These are building options, not a bundle you have to buy. The agreed scope determines what is included.

sections.heading: First understand the business. Then decide what to build.
paragraphs: The first conversation covers what you do, how customers reach you, how work gets delivered and where the team spends time chasing, copying or checking. Bring one recent job or customer enquiry and the tools involved.

If deeper discovery is needed, we agree that work and its cost separately. A business review can map the workflow, assess improvement opportunities and prioritise a first project. Before development, you receive a defined scope, deliverables, dependencies, cost and acceptance checks.

sections.heading: One useful improvement. Room to grow.
paragraphs: Start with the workflow creating the most friction. A first build might connect website enquiries to an opportunity dashboard. A later phase could add job handovers, a customer portal or more reporting when the need is clear.

You review the working system, test realistic situations and receive guidance for running it. Hosting, subscriptions, account ownership, maintenance and any ongoing support are discussed explicitly, so they don’t become surprises after launch.

faqs.question: Do I need to know which software I want?
faqs.answer: No. Start with what your business does, the tools you use and the work you want to improve. We assess whether an existing product, an integration or a custom build is the best fit.

faqs.question: What happens in the first business conversation?
faqs.answer: We discuss how customers find you, how enquiries and jobs move through the business, who does the work and where things get stuck. It is a fit and scoping conversation. A detailed audit or written roadmap is separately agreed work if needed.

faqs.question: Can you build the website and the admin dashboard together?
faqs.answer: Yes, where that fits the agreed project. We can connect public forms to private records, permissions, stages and actions. Existing websites and systems can also be reviewed for integration rather than automatically replaced.

faqs.question: Does every project need AI?
faqs.answer: No. A reliable rule or a simpler process may solve the problem better. AI is considered when interpretation, summarisation or knowledge retrieval has a useful role, with appropriate checks and data access.

faqs.question: How much does a connected business system cost?
faqs.answer: The cost depends on workflows, screens, integrations, permissions and data requirements. We define a first scope before quoting development. Discovery, hosting, software licences, maintenance and ongoing support are identified separately where relevant.

faqs.question: Can we start small and add more later?
faqs.answer: Yes. A first phase can focus on one valuable workflow. We consider future needs in the design without making you pay for every possible feature at the start.

faqs.question: What happens after the build?
faqs.answer: You receive the agreed handover covering everyday use, account ownership, dependencies and running the system. Any maintenance or ongoing support arrangement is separately agreed.

cta.label: Talk through your business
cta.heading: What are you tired of working around?
cta.text: Bring the repeated task, awkward spreadsheet or disconnected customer journey. Tell me how your business works today, and we’ll identify a sensible first improvement.

primaryIntent: custom business apps; business process review; connected websites and admin dashboards; business automation
summary: Start with a business review. Build the website, dashboard and automations your operation needs.

useCases.title: From new enquiry to booked work.
useCases.body: Capture the request, assign an owner, track the quote and carry agreed details into the job. See what needs a reply without reconstructing the inbox.

useCases.audience: Teams that deliver jobs or orders
useCases.title: Know what is ready. Know what is blocked.
useCases.body: Bring tasks, capacity and customer commitments into a shared view. Give each person the next action and surface the exceptions that need a decision.

useCases.title: Enter it once. Use it where it belongs.
useCases.body: Connect website forms, existing applications and internal records. Agree which system owns each field and how failed or duplicate updates are handled.

journey.heading: Follow one enquiry all the way into the job.
journey.example: Consider an installation business where website enquiries, quotes and job details are scattered across forms, inboxes and spreadsheets.
journey.question: Who needs a reply, and what should happen next?
scope: Owner, stage and dated next action
Agreed handover from quote to job
journey.boundary: Invoicing, payments, scheduling and customer portal features are separate decisions, included only when agreed.
build: Workflow · Hand over the agreed job

stages.label: Understand
stages.title: Walk through the work behind the website.
stages.body: We trace a recent enquiry from the first message to the completed job. We inspect where information lives, who handles it and where the team copies, chases or loses context.
stages.output: A workflow map, bottleneck list and clear starting problem.

stages.label: Agree
stages.title: Choose the first improvement worth building.
stages.body: The first phase captures enquiries, assigns owners, records next actions and carries accepted quote details into a job. We agree permissions, existing-system connections, cost and the situations used to check success.
stages.output: A prioritised first scope, proposed cost and acceptance checklist.

stages.label: Build
stages.title: Connect the customer journey to the working system.
stages.body: A public enquiry form connects to a private dashboard. The owner can review a request, record the next action and progress the opportunity. Approved job details move forward without asking the team to retype them.
stages.output: A reviewable website-to-dashboard workflow with defined access.

stages.label: Test
stages.title: Check the awkward cases before relying on it.
stages.body: We test normal enquiries, duplicate submissions, failed connections and account permissions. Alerts and recovery are checked so a broken link does not quietly leave the team believing work was done.
stages.output: Workflow, permission and failure-handling checks against agreed criteria.

stages.label: Hand over
stages.title: Make the system useful beyond launch day.
stages.body: You learn how to review enquiries, update the next action and handle exceptions. The handover records account ownership, hosting, dependencies, data responsibilities and any agreed support.
stages.output: A working guide, ownership record and running-cost overview.

tests.label: New request
tests.reason: Create one record, assign the agreed owner and make the next action visible.

tests.label: Duplicate
tests.reason: An agreed submission identifier prevents an accidental retry creating duplicate records.

tests.label: Connection fails
tests.reason: Do not show success without confirmed storage. Give a retry or alternate contact route and flag the issue.

handover.title: Use it every day
handover.body: Review requests, assign ownership, update stages and record the next action.

handover.title: Handle the exceptions
handover.body: Recognise failed updates, avoid duplicate work and follow the agreed recovery process.

handover.title: Know what you own
handover.body: Accounts, source code arrangements, hosting, subscriptions, data access and any agreed maintenance.
